extracted.intended_audience: self-regulatory organizations (exchanges), exchange counsel, market participants, and commenters to SEC rule filings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for filing and evaluating SRO (exchange) non-transaction fee rule changes (market data, connectivity, port fees), and for submitting public comments on those filings. Covers statutory tests, Staff Guidance expectations, disclosure/confidentiality practices, and procedural comment submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with the Exchange Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views, and arguments concerning whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission may summarily suspend the rule change within 60 days if it appears necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act; if suspended, the Commission will institute proceedings to determine whether to approve or disapprove the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory standards under 15 U.S.C. 78f(b) (including subsections cited)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rule changes must satisfy the requirements of Section 6(b) of the Exchange Act, as cited (15 U.S.C. 78f(b), including subsections 4, 5, and 8 referenced in the filing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced statutory provisions include, among other things, requirements related to fair competition, equitable allocation of dues/fees, and protection of investors; filers should demonstrate how the proposal meets these statutory obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not unfairly discriminatory (15 U.S.C. 78f(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees and fee structures must not be unfairly discriminatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exchange filings should explain why a proposed fee is not unfairly discriminatory (e.g., why no broker-dealer is required to become a member, why differential treatment is justified), and should consider whether competitive alternatives exist for participants who decline to pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a record and explain conclusions sufficient to enable review (Staff Guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filers relying on a cost-based approach should develop a record and explain their conclusions in a written decision sufficient to enable staff review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange argues that historical legacy filings should likewise have developed records and written explanations; the Staff Guidance expects exchanges to provide disclosures and justification that support the reasonableness of fees so staff can perform their review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff Guidance on SRO Rule Filings Relating to Fees — disclosure and justification expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Staff Guidance (May 21, 2019) requires improved disclosures and that exchanges justify that their market data and access fee proposals are fair and reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Staff Guidance serves to improve transparency, the Exchange contends it has made it difficult for non-legacy exchanges to adopt or increase fees; filers should follow the Staff Guidance but also seek clarity on its application and uniformity across exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-based approach — required cost disclosures and profit-margin rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: When a filer pursues a cost-based approach to justify fees, it must provide detailed cost information (including total costs related to third-party vendors) and supporting analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vendor cost information may be subject to confidentiality restrictions and provided to staff under separate cover. The Exchange requests that Staff be clear about what they determine is an appropriate profit margin if staff will judge profit margins as part of their review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market-based vs. cost-based review and historical precedent
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission historically applied a 'market-based' test in assessing market data fees, but recent Staff Guidance and the Revised Review Process emphasize more detailed cost/disclosure-based review for some filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filers should identify whether they are relying on a market-based rationale or a cost-based rationale, and provide the disclosures and analysis appropriate to that approach; applicants should be aware of potential disparate treatment between legacy and non-legacy exchanges and address comparability concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee parity as an alternative to avoid disparate treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: A fee parity alternative (i.e., parity between legacy and non-legacy exchanges) is presented as a possible way to avoid unfair and discriminatory effects of different review standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange suggests parity or comparable disclosure standards across exchanges to ensure fair competition; filers may propose parity-based structures or otherwise explain why different treatment is justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential treatment for vendor and sensitive cost information
rubrics_metrics.description: Vendor cost information and other sensitive financial data may be subject to confidentiality restrictions and can be provided to Commission staff under separate cover with a request for confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While detailed cost disclosures may be necessary for staff review, exchanges can and do provide such information confidentially; filers should state when materials are submitted under confidentiality and follow staff procedures for confidential submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparability and uniformity of disclosure across exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed disclosures by exchanges (e.g., cost-based justifications) should be consistent across all exchanges to promote fair and even competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange argues that if it provides extensive disclosures, similar levels of disclosure should be required or expected of other exchanges to avoid competitive imbalance; filers should explain their disclosure levels and why they are appropriate relative to peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 19(d) challengeability constraint (D.C. Circuit precedent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Per D.C. Circuit decisions cited (e.g., Nasdaq v. SEC, SIFMA decision), Section 19(d) is not available to challenge generally-applicable fee rules; to be challengeable under Section 19(d) a fee rule must be targeted at specific individuals or entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filers and commenters should be aware of the limits on judicial challenges under Section 19(d) when arguing about the reasonableness of generally-applicable fee rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive effects and impact on inter-market competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed fee changes should be evaluated for their effects on competition between legacy and non-legacy exchanges and on market participants' ability to compete and invest in systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange contends that the Revised Review Process has adversely affected inter-market competition by impeding non-legacy exchanges' ability to adopt/increase fees necessary to invest in infrastructure and innovate; filers should discuss competitive impacts and provide supporting data where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirements for comment submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested persons may submit comments electronically via the Commission's internet comment form or by email, or send paper comments in triplicate; all submissions should refer to the file number and be submitted by the stated deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include file number SR-EMERALD-2023-27 on subject line; use only one submission method to help Commission processing; submissions will be posted on the Commission's website and made available for public inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include personally identifiable information (PII) in comments / public posting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; submit only information you wish to make available publicly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection, and will withhold material in accordance with 5 U.S.C. 552 as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear definitions and fee schedule specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee filings should include clear definitions of terms used in the fee schedule (e.g., 'Full Service MEI Ports', 'Limited Service MEI Ports', 'Matching Engine', 'Member').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing includes definitional clarifications and ministerial changes to the fee schedule; clear definitions help staff and commenters understand the scope and impact of proposed fees and limitations (e.g., port limits per matching engine).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and timely updates to cost analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchanges frequently update their Cost Analysis as strategic initiatives change, costs increase or decrease, and market participant needs and trading activity change; filers should present recent cost analyses supporting the filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange notes it conducted its most recent Cost Analysis ahead of this filing and that cost allocations (e.g., hardware/software, network) should be explained; filers should disclose methodology for allocating shared costs among affiliated markets where relevant.
